% Fixture: glossaries
%
% Purpose: verify the makeglossaries workflow for glossary and acronym expansion.
%
% Expected maketex behaviour:
%   - Engine: pdflatex
%   - Passes: 2  (latex → makeglossaries → latex)
%   - Aux tools: makeglossaries
%   - Output: main.pdf
%
% Pass 1: latex writes raw glossary entries to main.glo and acronym entries to
%         main.acn via the glossaries package
% makeglossaries: runs xindy/makeindex on both files, producing main.gls + main.acr
% Pass 2: latex reads main.gls and main.acr, typesets the glossary; converges

\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[acronym, toc]{glossaries}

\makeglossaries

\newglossaryentry{latex}{
  name={\LaTeX},
  description={A document preparation system based on \TeX}
}

\newglossaryentry{tex}{
  name={\TeX},
  description={A typesetting system created by Donald Knuth}
}

\newacronym{pdf}{PDF}{Portable Document Format}
\newacronym{toc}{ToC}{Table of Contents}

\title{Glossaries Test}
\author{Test Fixture}
\date{2026-06-07}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\section{Introduction}
This document tests that \texttt{maketex} correctly orchestrates the
\texttt{makeglossaries} workflow. \Gls{latex} is built on top of \gls{tex}.
Output is produced as a \gls{pdf} \gls{pdf} file. The document also has a
\gls{toc}.

\printglossaries

\end{document}
